architecture_plan.impact_analysis: SUPRA is already a native SwiftUI application using NavigationSplitView, NavigationStack, ObservableObject stores, @StateObject ownership, and standalone View structs. The research recommendations target UIKit→SwiftUI migration (UIHostingController, navigation bridge), which is not applicable. However, a modernisation opportunity exists: migrate from ObservableObject+@Published to the iOS 18+ @Observable macro. This reduces boilerplate, improves performance via fine-grained observation, and eliminates @StateObject/@ObservedObject distinction. Stores (DecisionStore, MissionStore, ControlCenterStore) are the primary candidates. All are @MainActor final class ObservableObject — ideal targets for @Observable. The existing NavigationSplitView + NavigationStack routing via ExecutiveDestination enum is sound and needs no change. @ViewBuilder computed properties for sub-views should remain; extracting them into separate files is unnecessary. .onAppear usage should be audited and replaced with .task for async operations to prevent duplicate calls during re-renders.
architecture_plan.recommended_approach: Phase 1: Audit — identify all .onAppear closures used for async data loading across the 15 SwiftUI files; flag for .task migration. Phase 2: Observable migration — convert DecisionStore, MissionStore, ControlCenterStore from ObservableObject+@Published to @Observable macro one store at a time, updating dependent views to use @State (instead of @StateObject) and @Bindable (instead of @ObservedObject). Phase 3: .task migration — replace .onAppear async calls with .task { } in views where data loading occurs, adding cancellation-safe patterns. Phase 4: Snapshot testing — adopt swift-snapshot-testing for visual regression on migrated screens before/after each change. No navigation rewrite needed. No UIHostingController or UIKit bridge work is required since SUPRA is already SwiftUI-native.
regression_risks: @Observable macro requires iOS 17+, minimum deployment target must be verified
@State in parent views may not recreate child bindings the same way @StateObject did — child view identity and lifecycle differ between @StateObject ownership and @Observable + @State pattern
Observation machinery in @Observable tracks property reads at compile time; computed properties or lazy vars in stores may not trigger view updates as expected
.task { } cancellation on view disappearance may interrupt in-flight network requests that were previously started via .onAppear without cancellation, potentially leaving data in partial state
Simultaneous ObservableObject and @Observable stores in the same view hierarchy may cause inconsistent observation behaviour if a view observes both macros
Snapshot test reference images must be regenerated on any visual change, adding CI overhead during migration window
implementation_steps: Verify iOS deployment target >= 17 in project settings; if < 17, defer @Observable migration and proceed only with .task migration
Audit all .onAppear blocks in the 15 SwiftUI files; list each async call site and confirm it has a matching cancellation or .task replacement
Migrate DecisionStore from ObservableObject+@Published to @Observable macro; update DecisionInboxView to use @State(DecisionStore()) and DecisionDetailView to use @Bindable
Migrate MissionStore similarly; update MissionCenterView and MissionDetailView
Migrate ControlCenterStore similarly; update SupraControlCenterView and ContentView
Audit ExecutiveDestination enum — no change needed, but verify all navigation destinations still resolve after store observation change
Replace all identified .onAppear async calls with .task { } including cancellation handling
Add swift-snapshot-testing package dependency; write snapshot tests for each migrated view covering loading, populated, empty, and error states
Run full test suite and visual diff; fix any regressions in view identity or data flow
Commit migration with per-step granularity for bisection safety
